A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that S. Paratyphi A has the potential to become a resistant pathogen.
the fluoroquinolone resistance of Salmonella Paratyph A is associated with double mutation in DNA gyrase (Ser83→Gly, Asp87→Glu) and single mutation in topoismerase IV (Ser80→Phe).

the molecular analysis of the fluoroquinolone resistance in the Salmonella enterica Paratyphi A isolate from India showed the presence of a unique strain with a high level of resistance to ciproflaxin associated with double mutations at DNA gyrase subunits (Ser83 → Phe and Asp87 → Gly) and a single mutation at topoisomerase subunit (Ser80 → Arg) in the ParC subunit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emergence of high-level ciproflox-acin-resistant Salmonella Paratypi A strains with multiple mutations in DNA gyrase and topoisomerase is a threat to effective treatment of typhoid fever.
the molecular analysis of fluoroquinolone resistance in S. Paratyphi A should be performed to identify strains with high-level resistance and thus to guide treatment decisions.
fluoroquinolone resistance in S. Paratyphi A in India has emerged independently and has different molecular characteristics compared with the strains circulating in other regions of the world.
